prompt: Mariana asks what food you like now that you live in Bogotá. Text her back as a friend, in two short sentences: one thing you like and one you don't.

constraints.label: say what you like with me gusta or me gustan
include one thing you don't like
gustar works like "is pleasing to me": me gusta, not yo gusto

model: Me gustan las arepas con queso. No me gusta el picante.

prompt: You have finished eating at a restaurant and the waiter is across the room. Politely ask him (an older stranger you'd call usted) to bring the bill.

constraints.label: mention la cuenta
ask it as a question
usted, not tú

model: Disculpe, ¿nos trae la cuenta, por favor?

prompt: Vale wants to know your usual order at the café. Write her two short sentences about what you always order.

constraints.label: use pido (yo form of pedir)
pedir changes e to i: pido

model: Siempre pido ajiaco. Y con el ajiaco, pido una limonada.

prompt: You bought a juice for Vale and want to invite her to the market. Leave her a note, friendly, with the juice and the invitation.

constraints.label: use para ti, conmigo or contigo
include an invitation as a question
conmigo and contigo, not con mí or con ti

model: Este jugo es para ti. ¿Vienes conmigo al mercado?

prompt: Order a second drink from the waiter at a restaurant. He is an older stranger you'd call usted. Use one short sentence.

constraints.label: ask with me trae or me regala
use otro or otra
otro already means "another": no un or una

model: ¿Me trae otra limonada, por favor?

prompt: At a café counter, order for yourself to the server (an older stranger you'd call usted): a black coffee with no sugar and something with cheese.

constraints.label: use sin for "without"
use con for "with"
mention queso

model: Un tinto sin azúcar y una arepa con queso, por favor.

prompt: You are at the Paloquemao market. Ask the stallholder (an older man you would call usted) for a pound of tomatoes and half a dozen eggs.

constraints.label: use a container word + de (una libra de...)
mention huevos
ask politely as a question

model: ¿Me regala una libra de tomate y media docena de huevos?

prompt: Write a sign for the café door telling customers the rule: they pay first. Two short sentences, speaking to any customer as tú.

constraints.label: use hay que or tienes que
mention paying

model: Hay que pagar antes de comer. Tienes que esperar en la fila.

prompt: Tomás holds up a spoon and asks what it is for. Reply to him in one or two short sentences, as a friend.

constraints.label: use sirve para
what it is for: sirve para + verb or noun

model: Esta cuchara sirve para la sopa. Y esa sirve para el postre.

prompt: Text Mariana, a friend, to set up lunch at the café. Suggest a day and a time in one question.

constraints.label: use nos vemos
give a time with a las (or a la una)
ask it as a question

model: ¿Nos vemos el sábado a las doce en el café?

prompt: Tell Mariana, in two short sentences, what two other people at the café like to eat: Don Hernando and Vale.

constraints.label: use a [name] le gusta or le encanta
le goes before gusta

model: A don Hernando le encanta el ajiaco. A Vale le gustan los buñuelos.

prompt: You are ordering at a busy restaurant. Ask the waiter (older, you'd call usted) what he recommends, and say you want your food to go. Two short sentences.

constraints.label: ask ¿Qué me recomienda?
say para llevar
usted, not tú

model: ¿Qué me recomienda? Quiero una sopa para llevar.

prompt: Your friend Camilo asks what you want to eat tonight. Text him back, someone your age: say one dish you like and ask if he likes another.

constraints.label: say what you like with me gusta or me gustan
gustar works like "is pleasing to me": me gusta, not yo gusto

model: Me gusta el ajiaco. ¿Y te gustan las arepas?

prompt: Mariana asks if you and Vale like the same desserts. Text her two short sentences: what Vale likes and what Tomás likes.

constraints.label: say what Vale likes with a Vale le gusta
say what Tomás likes with a Tomás le gusta
keep the pronoun: a Vale le gusta

model: A Vale le gusta la torta. A Tomás le gustan las frutas.

prompt: You cannot meet Mariana for lunch today. Text her, as a friend, one sentence saying what you have to do, and one asking about tomorrow.

constraints.label: use tengo que plus an infinitive
tener que needs que before the verb

model: Hoy tengo que trabajar en el café. ¿Comemos mañana?

prompt: You are leaving a note for a new waiter at Rosa's café. In two short sentences, tell him one thing that must be done at every table (a general rule, not about him).

constraints.label: use hay que plus an infinitive for a general rule
hay que goes straight before the infinitive

model: Hay que llevar la carta a la mesa. Y hay que traer agua.

prompt: Describe to Mariana what you and a friend order at Rosa's café: your friend orders a cake and you order a coffee. Write one sentence, as a friend.

constraints.label: use pide for your friend
use pido for yourself
pedir changes e to i: pide, pido

model: Mi amigo pide una torta y yo pido un café.

prompt: A new friend your age is about to try Colombian restaurants. Text two short sentences: ask what he orders, and say what you always order.

constraints.label: use pides when asking him
use pido for yourself

model: ¿Qué pides tú en un restaurante? Yo siempre pido sopa.

prompt: You are at Rosa's café and Vale asks who the cake is for. Reply in two short sentences: it is for her, and you want to eat it with her.

constraints.label: use para ti after para
use contigo, not con ti
after con say contigo; after para say ti

model: La torta es para ti. Quiero comer contigo.

prompt: Mariana texts to ask about tonight's table at the café. Reply in two short sentences: the table is for you and Vale, and you are going with Vale (use a pronoun for her).

constraints.label: use para nosotros for the two of you
use con ella, not con Vale
after con or para use pronouns like ella, nosotros, ti, not tú

model: La mesa es para nosotros. Voy con ella.
